title: Our favorite apps for listening to music
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The Apple iPhone 16E
recommendations.blurb: I’m torn on this one. I like that it’s $599, I like that it has good battery life, I like that it has Face ID and USB-C. But only one camera? And an Action Button but no MagSafe?

recommendations.name: Avowed
recommendations.blurb: It’s been a while since an Xbox game felt like it was everywhere on my social feeds. But it seems like everyone’s into Avowed, a properly huge and complicated RPG that, according to my colleague Andrew Webster, doesn’t blow up the format but executes it well.

recommendations.name: Memes & Nightmares
recommendations.blurb: A satirical true crime documentary! About a meme that was everywhere and then suddenly disappeared! It’s giving Documentary Now! and American Vandal, except about NBA Twitter and GIFs. Truly the intersection of all my interests.

recommendations.name: The Americas
recommendations.blurb: There are few things in the world I enjoy more than the Planet Earth series. I watch them all, I watch all the copycats, I only wish there were more of them. And now I get a version of it in my own backyard! With Tom Hanks narrating! That’s my Sunday nights sorted for a while.

recommendations.name: The Oppo Find N5
recommendations.blurb: A foldable phone I’ll likely never be able to buy but will lust after nonetheless. It’s impossibly thin, outrageously expensive, and a genuinely exciting sign that foldable design can continue to go cool places.

recommendations.name: The King Jim Pomera DM250US
recommendations.blurb: I have long had romantic ideas about buying a digital typewriter and just buggering off to some Airbnb in the woods to write. This one, from Japanese stationary brand King Jim, is pretty expensive but has a good track record in Japan and looks alarmingly close to the device I’d want it to be.

recommendations.name: Grand Theft Hamlet
recommendations.blurb: A documentary, now streaming on Mubi, about two actors who decided, during the pandemic, to… do all of Hamlet inside of GTA. (Look, we all got weird during covid.) The whole thing takes place inside the game, and the gimmick actually really works.

recommendations.name: Sober Ringtones
recommendations.blurb: This one is specifically for my mother-in-law (hi, Diane!) who has the most ear-splitting ringtone of all time. In her defense, all built-in ringtone options suck. I think you’re a monster if your phone is on anything but vibrate, but I like the sound of these chiller, more melodic options.

recommendations.name: BBC Radiophonic Workshop
recommendations.blurb: I confess I knew nothing about the Radiophonic Workshop until I saw this new library of their work appear online, but wow is there a cool (and decades-long) history to this pioneering group of electronic musicians. I’d bet you start to hear some of these old-school sounds show up all over, and soon.

recommendations.name: Spotify
recommendations.blurb: Spotify is the clear leader here. Apple Music was a pretty close second though, and the Apple Music users seem a lot happier than the Spotify users… The funniest thing I heard over and over was “I tried YouTube Music because I get it for free, but it’s not very good.” Which, same. I feel you.

recommendations.name: Tidal
recommendations.blurb: You know what got the most effusive love? Tidal! Tidal’s audio quality was a differentiator for a lot of folks, as was the fact that it’s an app for music and music only. I’m good on podcasts with Pocket Casts, personally, and have been convinced to give Tidal a real try.

recommendations.name: Bandcamp
recommendations.blurb: For buying music, Bandcamp and Discogs both came up a bunch. A few of you also like using Discogs’ collection-tracking stuff, which looks pretty cool.

recommendations.name: Plexamp
recommendations.blurb: Plexamp and Roon both came up a lot as a way to manage and access your music collection from anywhere. ( Supersonic also has some fans.) Plexamp in particular was probably the most-recommended piece of software in my inbox this week.

recommendations.name: Astiga
recommendations.blurb: There’s also Astiga, which I heard from a few folks is a useful single-player streaming service. Just dump some files somewhere, and stream them on your phone.

recommendations.name: Albums
recommendations.blurb: There are a few Apple-only apps that people really liked for managing their Apple Music collections: Albums makes everything feel like a CD collection again, Marvis makes everything crazy customizable, and one person described MusicBox as “a read later app for music.”

recommendations.name: XLD
recommendations.blurb: XLD and Exact Audio Copy got a lot of love as a way to rip CDs, and Mp3tag seems to be a great way to manage all kinds of tags and metadata.

recommendations.name: MacBook Pro with an M1 Max chip
recommendations.blurb: The computer: MacBook Pro with an M1 Max chip. I make music with lots of sample libraries that require a lot of RAM and CPU. It was stupid expensive but game-changing for making large audio productions.

recommendations.name: Descript
recommendations.blurb: Descript: The only way we manage to make a podcast.

recommendations.name: Ableton Live
recommendations.blurb: Ableton Live: My main Digital Audio Workstation for scoring and sound design.

recommendations.name: Audio Hijack
recommendations.blurb: Audio Hijack: This lets me capture audio from any source and record it.

recommendations.name: Loopback
recommendations.blurb: Loopback: This is like a digital mixer that lets me send audio from anywhere to anywhere so I can play music over Zoom, etc.

recommendations.name: Fission
recommendations.blurb: Fission: The lightest-weight, easiest-to-use audio editor.

recommendations.name: TickTick
recommendations.blurb: TickTick: My to-do list for everything.

recommendations.name: Apple Notes
recommendations.blurb: Apple Notes: I am a Notes power user and have it organize my entire life: every thought, script, note, song, whatever.

recommendations.name: Major Labels: A History of Popular Music in Seven Genres
recommendations.blurb: I am on my third read through Major Labels: A History of Popular Music in Seven Genres by Kelefa Sanneh.

recommendations.name: Taper’s Choice
recommendations.blurb: I am listening to Taper’s Choice.

recommendations.name: Bogdan in the Forest
recommendations.blurb: My kids and I watch the YouTube channel Bogdan in the Forest.

recommendations.name: Elektron Rytm MKII
recommendations.blurb: I am obsessed with the Elektron Rytm MKII and the UDO Super 6.

recommendations.name: UDO Super 6
recommendations.blurb: I am obsessed with the Elektron Rytm MKII and the UDO Super 6.

recommendations.name: the Framework event
recommendations.blurb: I’m super excited for the Framework event on the 25th. I picked up a 13-inch Intel Core Ultra laptop when it launched last year and have been loving it. Big fan of Framework’s mission, and I hope this event brings even more people to their products.

recommendations.name: 13-inch Intel Core Ultra laptop
recommendations.blurb: I’m super excited for the Framework event on the 25th. I picked up a 13-inch Intel Core Ultra laptop when it launched last year and have been loving it. Big fan of Framework’s mission, and I hope this event brings even more people to their products.

recommendations.name: Invincible
recommendations.blurb: I’m a big fan of the animated series Invincible on Amazon Prime, which just kicked off its third season.

recommendations.name: The comic
recommendations.blurb: I’m a big fan of the animated series Invincible on Amazon Prime, which just kicked off its third season.

recommendations.name: start of the semiconductor industry
recommendations.blurb: These days I’m reading about the history of Silicon Valley, especially about the start of the semiconductor industry.

recommendations.name: Obsidian
recommendations.blurb: I did a deep dive into Obsidian this week and ended up moving all my Apple Notes over to it. I’m particularly excited about the Graph and Canvas features. It’s like having a second brain. I don’t want to be dramatic, but this might have changed my life.

recommendations.name: Eusexua
recommendations.blurb: After the ridiculous enjoyable new album of FKA Twigs — ‘ Eusexua ’ — I discovered two additional Eusexua World Apple Music mixes curated by Koreless and FKA Twigs. Worth a listen. More to come apparently.

recommendations.name: Apple Music mixes
recommendations.blurb: After the ridiculous enjoyable new album of FKA Twigs — ‘ Eusexua ’ — I discovered two additional Eusexua World Apple Music mixes curated by Koreless and FKA Twigs. Worth a listen. More to come apparently.

recommendations.name: Civ VI
recommendations.blurb: I know Civ VII is the new hotness, but I learned this week with a Netflix account you can play Civ VI on your phone. It’s a crazy platform for Civ, and amazing it works, but why not break up some doomscrolling by being slaughtered by barbarians that are tougher than you remember?

recommendations.name: Tldraw
recommendations.blurb: I’m using Tldraw a lot lately — been loving it. It’s basically an infinite canvas but cooler. I really recommend it.

recommendations.name: KDE Neon
recommendations.blurb: Right now, I’m trying out Linux ( KDE Neon for its looks and customization). It definitely takes more time to make it work, but not as much as I feared. I’m positively surprised with its snappiness and better battery life (primarily in sleep mode) compared to Windows.

recommendations.name: Why Chess Strategy Changes Every Year
recommendations.blurb: I found this great Half as Interesting video about the evolution of what you might call “mainstream chess strategy” and was riveted by it.
